name: Cup
group: Things people make > Things in the house > Things to eat and drink with

features.claim: A cup has a flattened half-sphere shape.
features.quote: typically with a flattened hemispherical shape

features.claim: A cup holds about 6 to 16 US fluid ounces.
features.quote: often with a capacity of about 6–16 US fluid ounces (177–473 ml)

features.claim: A cup can be made of pottery, glass, metal, wood, stone, plastic or other materials.
features.quote: Cups may be made of pottery (including porcelain), glass, metal, wood, stone, polystyrene, plastic, lacquerware, or other materials.

features.claim: Modern household cups usually have no stem.
features.quote: Modern household shapes of cups generally lack a stem

quote_not_in_the_page.claim: A cup has an open mouth.

second_reading.claim: A cup is a small container for holding liquids to drink.
second_reading.quote: A cup is a small container used to hold liquids for drinking

second_reading.claim: A cup is brought to the mouth to drink from it.
second_reading.quote: Normally, a cup is brought in contact with the mouth for drinking

second_reading.claim: What counts as a real cup is not fixed and has changed between generations.
second_reading.quote: The definition of a cup is fluid
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Some people expect a cup to be porcelain with a handle and saucer, while others do not.
second_reading.quote: the "older generation" expected a cup to be made of porcelain and have both a handle and a saucer, so that the plastic cup with neither a handle, nor a saucer, was not a "real cup", while the "younger generation" made no such distinction
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Cups, mugs and glasses are near-synonyms, though they can be told apart.
second_reading.quote: cups, mugs and glasses are "near-synonyms", although "sufficient differences" can be found that divide them into different groups
